Prevention: Prevention measures are particularly important as this weed is difficult to control.
Tubers are the main means of spread; Clean tools and farm machinery to prevent introduction to new fields
Do not accept potentially contaminated materials, e.g. soil on planting stock
Plant highly competitive cover or cash crops such as jack bean, velvet bean, bush bean, soybean, cotton, chayote and cucumber.
Narrow crop row spacing can help prevent the establishment of the weed by shading it
Control established populations near waterways to prevent spread during flooding and storm events
Monitoring: Erect, perennial sedge (30-60 cm high), with extensive underground network composed of tubers
Tubers dark brown/black, irregular shaped, 1-2 cm long at maturity, with several buds
Leaves linear with distinct midrib, 7 mm wide
Inflorescence with several unequal 'branches', each 2-6 cm long, emerging from the tip of the stem; each with 3-8 purplish-brown flowerheads
Direct Control: Destroy tubers and rhizomes in the soil via dessication (most effective in dry soil) or exhausting food reserves
Cultivate every 2-3 weeks until crop canopy forms: the weed is shade intolerant
Plough and cover an infested area with a polyethylene sheet to destroy tubers and rhizomes in the dry season (soil solarization).
This can be very effective but not always 100%.
Place organic mulch over areas where weed is expect to grow to provide temporary weed suppression
Tillage must be deep (> 12cm) in order to disturb as many of the rhizomes as possible.
Do this every three weeks and under dry conditions so the exposed rhizomes dessicate.
